HEAD_RESOLVED_SLICE_DA_270_RULING.rule: sorting is not ordering until the key is unique. The slice is built from HEAD-RESOLVED records -- supersession FIRST so each slug appears exactly once, THEN sort BY SLUG. Order is derived from the resolved key, never from file position.
HEAD_RESOLVED_SLICE_DA_270_RULING.head_rule: greatest recv_ns wins (append-only); a TIE REFUSES BY SLUG (SLUG_HAS_TWO_HEADS_AFTER_RESOLUTION)
HEAD_RESOLVED_SLICE_DA_270_RULING.duplicates_are_counted: PRE_RESOLUTION_DUPLICATE_SLUGS -- counted and named, never silently deduped

2026-09-07.reason: NOT duplicates -- it has none. The landed instrument sorts LINES, and a line begins `{"recv_ns":...`, so LINE ORDER IS recv_ns ORDER, not slug order. The ruling orders by the resolved key. Same 2,016 records, different ordering, different digest.
2026-09-07.I_ASSERTED_THE_OPPOSITE_FIRST: my falsifier cell asserted 09-07 would be UNCHANGED because it has no duplicates. The cell FAILED and it was right to -- I had reasoned about duplicates and missed that the ordering key itself moved.

2026-09-09.reason: BOTH causes. 09-09 holds 2,030 lines for the day but only 2,016 DISTINCT slugs -- 14 slugs appear twice, each a `gave_up` stub (closed: null, winners: null) followed at a LATER recv_ns by the real resolution. THE UNRESOLVED SLICE COUNTED A GIVE-UP BESIDE ITS OWN SUPERSESSION, which is not the day's settled state.

HEAD_RESOLVED_SLICE_DA_270_RULING.CONSEQUENCE_FOR_CONSUMERS: every slice digest published before this ruling is superseded. A consumer enforcing slice identity on the old numbers will refuse a correct receipt. DE has been told directly.

FIX_2_the_receipt_COMPUTES_its_own_slice.why: there is now nothing for a caller to get wrong; the identity is not an argument.
